**Incident Handoff — Gateway 503s**

**Root cause:** Deploy `dep-4471` (gateway, a.novak, "config: connection-per-request for pool isolation", ran 2026-03-14 02:12:00Z–02:14:00Z) flipped config `gateway.pool.perRequest` from `false` to `true` (also bumped `gateway.timeout.upstreamMs` 2000→2500). This stopped connection reuse against a fixed pool size of 20, and the pool saturated within seconds of the deploy finishing.

**Impact window:** 2026-03-14T02:14:18.972Z (first `503`, req-07401) through at least 2026-03-14T03:59:27.974Z (last line in `logs/gateway.log`) — **still active/unresolved at log cutoff**, no recovery observed. Error rate did not decay; `waiting` queue on the pool grew from 13 to 74 over that span.

**Signature error:**
```
ERROR access  req-07401 /v1/cart -> billing-svc 503 659ms
ERROR pool    req-07401 ERR_POOL_EXHAUSTED acquiring connection from pool (size 20, in_use 20, waiting 13)
```
Affected routes: `/v1/cart`, `/v1/session`, `/v1/catalog/search`, `/v1/orders`, `/v1/checkout`, across all downstream services (orders-svc, billing-svc, catalog-svc, accounts-svc). `/health` checks stayed 200 throughout — LB/health-check likely blind to this.

**Scope:** Gateway only. `logs/worker.log` was checked for the same window (01:00–03:59Z) — clean, no pool exhaustion, no 503, one unrelated pre-existing slow-query warning (OPS-2210). Not a shared-infra/DB-wide issue.

**Action: roll back `dep-4471`** (revert `gateway.pool.perRequest` to `false`, generation 119→118). Other deploys in window (dep-4472 billing-svc, dep-4473 catalog-svc) are unrelated and can stay.
